question: Does restricting pretrained-encoder updates improve generalization relative to late-stage full tuning?

changes.frozen: Freeze all original encoder parameters; train unchanged UPer64.
changes.lora8: Freeze all original encoder parameters; rank8 alpha8 native LoRA on late Mamba in/out projections, attention qkv/proj, and every late-block MLP fc1/fc2. Train unchanged UPer64.

lora.init: Native Kaiming A and zero B; isolated CPU seed142; original weights retained exactly.

training.loss: unchanged BCE + per-image soft Dice with original soft masks
training.encoder_mode: eval throughout; LoRA gradients enabled; no dropout or merge on eval
training.initial_encoder: Official ImageNet pretrained MambaVision-S; not a segmentation checkpoint
training.initialization: Common seed42 UPer64 head state exact

reference: Completed Stage45 UPer64; exact762validation replay before reuse.
selection: Maximum validation macro Dice with earliest tie; complete100epochs. All arms trained before fixed867test per arm.
interpretation_limits: Single seed pilot, not novel method or full MambaPEFT reproduction.
Fixed rank, fixed placement, same encoder LR as reference; no LoRA-specific hyperparameter optimization. Failure does not exclude all PEFT.
Frozen vs LoRA tests adaptation package; original versus LoRA changes update subspace and trainable parameter count.
No patient-disjointness guarantee; exposed test is not untouched confirmation.

evidence.training_pattern: Training loss continues falling after best-validation epoch; overfitting is a hypothesis, not established unique cause.
evidence.previous_freezing: Earlier Swin experiments favored late fine-tuning over fully frozen in two seeds; matched UPer64 control needed.

software: Pinned microsoft/LoRA Linear used without edits or installation; Sony MambaPEFT informs research question only.
